chunks.text: 21-year-old male, Professional, resident of Clementi, Singapore.
Salbutamol Inhaler 2 puffs as needed PRN.
Salbutamol Inhaler 2 puffs as needed PRN.
General Anesthesia with Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Nerve Block

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning! I'm going to go over some questions to make sure we're all set for your surgery today. First, can you tell me a bit about why you're having this knee surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, yes. I've been having a lot of pain in my left knee, especially when I bend it. The doctor said there's a torn meniscus, so they need to go in and clean it up with the arthroscopy lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for sharing that. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and has it been affecting your daily activities?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: About six months now. It's been getting worse, especially when I walk or climb stairs. I can't exercise like I used to, which is frustrating because I try to stay active.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. Now, let's go over your medications. You're currently taking Montelukast 10 mg daily and using a Salbutamol Inhaler as needed. And you've stopped Atorvastatin 20 mg daily?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, that's right. I take the Montelukast every evening for my asthma, and the inhaler when I need it. I stopped the Atorvastatin a few weeks ago as advised.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Got it. Now, regarding allergies — your records say 'no known allergies', but I always like to confirm directly. Have you ever had any reactions to medications, foods, or other substances like latex?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, actually, I think I do have a latex allergy. I found out during a previous check-up. When I had a glove on my hand, my skin got really itchy and red. The doctor said it was a confirmed latex allergy.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that — it's very important for us to know. We'll make sure all the staff are aware and use latex-free equipment. Now, have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia before?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time. I've never been under general anesthesia before, so I'm a bit nervous about that part.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's completely normal. We'll make sure you're comfortable and explain everything beforehand. Now, are you NPO — that is, have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I stopped eating and drinking after midnight, like the instructions said. Just a bit thirsty now, but I'm managing.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great, thank you. Lastly, how would you describe your overall fitness level? Are you able to walk up a flight of stairs or do light housework without getting overly short of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can walk up stairs, but I do get a bit breathless, especially if I go too fast. My asthma is mild, and I only use the inhaler when I'm exercising or if it's dusty.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for all that information. We'll make sure your asthma is well-controlled during the procedure. We're planning for general anesthesia with a femoral nerve block to help with pain after surgery. Any questions from your side?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that covers it. I'm just ready to get this done and start recovering.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. We'll take good care of you. You'll meet the anesthesiologist shortly, and they'll go over the nerve block and anesthesia plan in more detail. Feel free to ask any questions then too.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] ultrasound-guided femoral nerve block, twenty milliliters of bupivacaine zero point five percent

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] heart rate increased to one hundred ten, gave five milligrams of labetalol

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] two liters of lactated ringers administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:40] systolic blood pressure dropped to ninety, gave one milligram of phenylephrine

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm okay, I guess. Still a bit sleepy, but my knee doesn't hurt too much.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Can you rate your pain for me, out of 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe a 3 or 4. There's some soreness, but it's manageable.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or feeling like you might be sick?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I feel fine. No dizziness or anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. How's your breathing? Any discomfort or tightness in your chest?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I'm breathing fine. A bit more aware of my breathing, but it's okay.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: You mentioned you have mild asthma. Any wheezing or shortness of breath at all?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing like that. I didn't even need my inhaler today.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. And just to check, do you remember the surgery being done?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yeah, I remember waking up and being moved here. It's a bit fuzzy, but I know what happened.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for confirming. We'll keep an eye on your pain and breathing, especially with your asthma and weight, but you're looking good so far.

claims.text: 21-year-old male
Elective Arthroscopic Knee Meniscectomy (Left) planned
General Anesthesia with Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Nerve Block planned
Currently taking Montelukast 10 mg daily
Currently using Salbutamol Inhaler 2 puffs as needed PRN
Stopped taking Atorvastatin 20 mg daily a few weeks ago as advised
Confirmed latex allergy with skin reaction (itching and redness) upon exposure
No known drug allergies recorded in GP summary, but patient did not report any during interview beyond latex
NPO since midnight as instructed for surgery
Mild asthma, only requires Salbutamol Inhaler during exercise or in dusty environments, no recent exacerbations reported
No previous surgeries or anesthesia, first time under general anesthesia
Left ankle fracture in 2018, healed and not relevant to current anesthesia plan
At 08:00, propofol 120 milligrams was administered for induction.
At 08:02, endotracheal tube was placed with a grade one view.
At 08:05, ultrasound-guided femoral nerve block with 20 milliliters of bupivacaine 0.5% was administered.
At 08:10, heart rate increased to 110 beats per minute, and 5 milligrams of labetalol was administered.
At 08:15, 2 liters of lactated ringers were administered.
At 08:40, systolic blood pressure dropped to 90 millimeters of mercury, and 1 milligram of phenylephrine was administered.

PONV risk due to multiple factors including opioid use (though not explicitly mentioned, common in post-op for pain management), female gender (not applicable here but considered for general risk), and history of motion sickness or nausea with prior anesthesia (not mentioned, but as a first-time patient under general anesthesia, baseline risk exists). However, the primary concern here is the use of propofol for induction, which can contribute to PONV.

Airway watch is necessary due to the patient's mild asthma history, which may increase the risk of bronchospasm or airway reactivity post-extubation. Although the patient has not had recent exacerbations, the use of general anesthesia and endotracheal intubation can trigger bronchospasm.

Glycemic control may be a concern given the patient's history of prediabetes (resolved), indicating a potential for impaired glucose metabolism. While not directly impacting the immediate post-op period, monitoring is prudent to prevent hyperglycemia, especially in the context of surgical stress and potential steroid administration (not mentioned but possible in some protocols).

Analgesia management is crucial due to the femoral nerve block with bupivacaine, which provides initial pain control but may wear off. Monitoring for adequate pain relief and potential need for supplemental analgesia is important to prevent discomfort and its associated complications.

Hemodynamic watch is necessary due to intraoperative fluctuations in blood pressure and heart rate. The patient experienced tachycardia (HR 110 bpm) and hypotension (SBP 90 mmHg), which were managed with labetalol and phenylephrine, respectively. Post-operative monitoring is essential to ensure hemodynamic stability is maintained.

Latex allergy management to prevent anaphylactic reaction. The patient has a confirmed latex allergy with skin reaction (itching and redness) upon exposure, necessitating strict avoidance of latex-containing products in the post-operative setting.
21-year-old male undergoing elective arthroscopic knee meniscectomy on the left side under general anesthesia with ultrasound-guided femoral nerve block.
Patient has a confirmed latex allergy with skin reaction, is currently taking Montelukast and using a Salbutamol Inhaler as needed. No previous surgeries or anesthesia.
Intraoperative events included tachycardia managed with labetalol and hypotension managed with phenylephrine. A femoral nerve block with bupivacaine was administered for pain control.

Monitor for hemodynamic stability due to intraoperative fluctuations, watch for signs of PONV given propofol use, ensure strict latex avoidance, and manage analgesia as the nerve block may wear off. Also, consider airway watch due to mild asthma history.
Patient reports pain level of 3 or 4 out of 10, describing it as manageable soreness.
Patient denies any nausea or feeling of impending sickness post-operatively.
Patient reports no dizziness and is breathing fine, with only increased awareness of breathing.
Patient confirms no wheezing or shortness of breath and did not require inhaler use on the day of surgery.
Patient has partial recall of the surgery, remembering waking up and being moved to recovery, but details are fuzzy.
Patient is a 21-year-old male, undergoing elective arthroscopic knee meniscectomy (left) with general anesthesia and ultrasound-guided femoral nerve block.
Patient's current medications include Montelukast 10 mg daily and Salbutamol Inhaler as needed, both continued into the post-operative period.
Patient has a confirmed latex allergy, with previous reaction of itchiness and redness upon contact, requiring latex-free equipment.

Given your use of Montelukast and Salbutamol Inhaler, do you have a history of asthma or reactive airway disease that has not been explicitly documented?
